Dismissed: the destructured slot is _parameters with the merged list in let parameters (PHP retypes in place, as parsePipeString's note records); array_merge([passable, stack], parameters) is Arr.merge, the same language compensation as Arr.pad/Arr.reverse; the ternary is token for token through the helpers -- methodExists (method_exists; a method here is a function-valued field reached through __index), callMethod ($pipe->{$this->method}(...$parameters), the explicit target being the self PHP passes implicitly) and call ($callable(...$args)) -- so no local and no cast survives at the site. Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#parsePipe.note: The upstream line itself: [name, parameters] destructured from Arr.pad(Str.explode(':', pipe, 2), 2, undefined) -- explode and array_pad are language compensations (extra members on Str/Arr, docblocked), and the undefined pad is the identity a Luau array forces, with the missing slot destructuring to undefined and playing is_null. The is_null branch is upstream's if/else and the return is the single [name, parameters]. Dismissed: the string slot destructures as _parameters under the underscore convention (the same spelling _pipes uses) -- PHP retypes $parameters from string to array in place, a TS binding's type is fixed at declaration, so the retyped half lives in let parameters; the exact-same-name encoding does compile but costs a tuple annotation plus a cast on the declaration, judged not worth it. The contract is upstream's (string in), and the port's non-string carriers ([Class, ...args], a bare class) live in splitPipe() in Pipeline/helpers.ts, dispatched where carry() resolves the pipe; both parsers feed make(), whose Abstract union plays the DI role PHP's string plays. Known scope difference for subclasses: an override of parsePipeString sees only string pipes here (in PHP every parameterized pipe is a string); one that needs every carrier overrides carry(), as it would upstream.
